recall_prompt: Say how you would find 50 C n when n C 21 equals n C 27.
insider_note: The lower numbers 21 and 27 are unequal, so only the sum branch applies: n = 21 + 27 = 48. The question is finished at ⁵⁰C₄₈ = ⁵⁰C₂ = 1225, not at n — and the C₂ rewrite is what keeps the arithmetic to two factors.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₛ ⇒ r = s or r + s = n
steps.margin_note: First mark. State the identity. 21 ≠ 27, so n = 21 + 27 = 48.
lines: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₛ ⇒ r = s or r + s = n

recall.must_convey: That n C r equals n C s means r equals s or r plus s equals n, and since 21 is not 27, n = 48.
accept: n C r equals n C s means r is s or r plus s is n, twenty one is not twenty seven so n is forty eight
the two lower numbers add to n so n is forty eight
n is twenty one plus twenty seven which is forty eight
lower numbers add cheste n forty eight
use the rule that the lower numbers add up to n

steps.why: Two different lower numbers give the same ⁿC value only when they add to n, because ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ. That one line replaces any attempt to expand ⁿC₂₁.
common_mistakes: Writing n = 48 without stating the identity.
Subtracting instead of adding: 27 − 21 = 6 is not n.

steps.label: Evaluate ⁵⁰C₄₈

recall.must_convey: That 50 C 48 is 50 C 2, which is 50 times 49 over 2 = 1225.
accept: fifty C forty eight is fifty C two which is fifty into forty nine by two equals one thousand two hundred twenty five
fifty C forty eight equals fifty C two equals twelve twenty five
fifty C forty eight ni fifty C two ga rasi twelve twenty five
heard_as: one thousand two hundred twenty five

steps.why: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ turns 48 factors into 2. The number 1225 is the answer; the symbol ⁵⁰C₄₈ is not.
common_mistakes: Computing 50 · 49 = 2450 and forgetting to halve it.
